contexts.text: (Lot) lingered () = resistance from the nature of evil. Explained.
Stay not in all the plain = that he should not delay in anything of them.

Thou shalt tarry with him some days () = what is successive; (for) to tarry has a similar signification to to dwell; thus it = to live; but to tarry is predicated of the life of truth with good; and to dwell, of the life of good with truth.
Concerning this Successive, or the tarrying of Jacob with Laban, it treats in what follows.
I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed until now () = that he had imbued the good signified by Laban... To stay or tarry is predicated of the life of truth with good; here, = to imbue.
The sojourning and tarrying of Jacob with Laban.
And tarry there () = life. To tarry or dwell = life.
A certain Spirit came to me, inquiring whether I knew where he might stay...
They were driven out of Egypt, and could not tarry () = that they were removed by those who were in falsity from evil... Not to be able to tarry = the necessity of removal.
The tarrying of the Sons of Israel in Egypt = the infestation of the spiritual...
(Married partners there) tarry together a longer or shorter time... But if love truly conjugial... has not conjoined them, after some tarrying, they are separated.
Some (are carried to Heaven) after a short tarrying with good Spirits.
They are not allowed, as before, to delay in the World of Spirits...
Some stay in the World of Spirits a month or a year, and some ten years and up to thirty... but at this day, not beyond twenty years.
That which is from the body in the spirit does not last long; but the love which is from the spirit in the body does last.
The wolf shall tarry with the lamb () = ... It will tarry = a state of peace...
By tarrying and cooperation (with the Lord)...
